Summary: Bab-Gathon has stood on the Sarru through three sieges, held less by the temple's gods than by one mortal man the city has quietly decided must be touched by something divine. He isn't. He is simply very good at not dying. Bruce has survived three sieges by refusing to believe in gods. Then one shows up. entry.title: Retrograde
entry.summary:
Author: Holdt

Rating: ExplicitLanguage: EnglishWords: 134,804Chapters: 14/20Kudos: 53

Summary: A dangerous serial killer is on the loose. How will Bruce catch them when he can't remember what happened only moments ago? Bruce Wayne wakes with anterograde amnesia—twelve minutes of retention, then reset. He can't form new long-term memories, can't remember the last conversation, can't verify his own identity beyond what documentation tells him. Clark Kent loves him anyway. Loves him forty-seven times over, each reset a new choice to trust evidence instead of memory. But when renowned neuroscientist Dr. Harrison Wells is murdered using the same extraction methodology that killed twelve others, all evidence points to Bruce Wayne. Fingerprints on the equipment. DNA under the victim's fingernails. Nine hours of missing time he can't account for. Bruce doesn't remember killing him. But he doesn't remember not killing him either. Told in dual timelines—color chapters moving backward through Bruce's life with amnesia, black-and-white chapters moving forward through the investigation that preceded it—RETROGRADE is a psychological thriller about identity without memory, trust without verification, and what it means to be Batman when you can't remember being Batman.

entry.title: Turn This Manor into a Home!
entry.summary:
Author: jerrys_21_sided_die

Rating: General AudiencesLanguage: EnglishWords: 8,415Chapters: 5/?Kudos: 34

Summary: For as long as Bruce can (or chooses) to remember, Wayne Manor has been empty. After Alfred gets fed up with his macho “I’m Batman I don’t need anyone but the night.” attitude he sends Bruce to Haly’s circus to unwind; but thats not what happens, Bruce watches two performers fall to their deaths as their 7 year old son watches. Bruce decides right there and then he won’t let Richard become one of the children lost to Gothams foster care system. Along the way a reporter from the Daily Planet catches wind of this ordeal, as he interviews Richard (with the help of Bruce) he starts to linger more and more around Wayne Manor. As introverted as Bruce is, he likes the reporters company, Richard’s little feet pattering around the manor, and the dinner outings the trio go on every Friday. They make this house (or mansion) a home.
